data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"Resumability reduces to a single atomicity invariant: the event-append and the budget-decrement must be a single atomic transaction. A halted run is resumable iff the persisted state is the result of a sequence of completed transactions\u2014each one either fully committed (event written + budget decremented + digest linked) or fully rolled back (neither persisted). Resumption must be refused iff the transaction log shows a split: an event persisted without a matching budget decrement, or a budget decrement without a matching event, or a partially committed transaction (event bytes present but digest not finalized).","counterconditions":[{"case":"The system does not implement atomic append-and-decrement, so a halt can split the transaction, leaving an event without a budget update or vice versa.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The storage layer does not support atomic multi-key updates (event + budget + digest), making the invariant unenforceable.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"A torn write occurs despite atomicity guarantees due to storage-level corruption (disk error, OS crash mid-flush).","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The budget accounting is approximate or lazy (e.g., estimated token counts adjusted later), so the decrement is not a precise atomic counterpart to the event.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Treat (append_event, decrement_budget, finalize_digest) as one ACID transaction. If the system guarantees this atomicity\u2014e.g., via a write-ahead log with two-phase commit or a single atomic store operation\u2014then any halt, even a crash, leaves the persisted state at a consistent transaction boundary. The next run simply reads the last committed transaction and continues. The append-only identity is preserved because every committed event has a finalized digest linking to its predecessor, and no partial transactions leave orphaned state. Refusal is required exactly when the atomicity guarantee was violated by the halt: the transaction was split across the crash boundary.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
